target_claim: In the second eqn block the proof asserts f^\to \circ f^\gets = (f^\gets \circ f^\to) \circ id_{P(T)}, citing 'Identity Mapping is Right Identity', and then applies 'Composition of Mappings is Associative' to turn (f^\gets \circ f^\to) \circ (f^\to \circ (f^\to)^{-1}) into ((f^\to \circ f^\gets) \circ f^\to) \circ (f^\to)^{-1}. Both steps silently swap the order of the composite f^\gets \circ f^\to, and the cited right-identity theorem's precondition (the identity must be on the domain of the mapping it postcomposes) fails.
